sentences.A4: We give a maximum-likelihood based algorithm for the estimation of its parameters, and we show how a fit of our model to two axially isolated point source measurements in an experimental setup can be used to accurately reproduce measured PSFs within the entire specimen.
sentences.T0: An accurate PSF model with few parameters for axially shift-variant deconvolution

title: An accurate PSF model with few parameters for axially shift-variant deconvolution

sentences.A0: The scale of participation on social news sites has challenged community managers, leaving them unable to detect and remove all inappropriate content by hand.
sentences.A1: Automated insult and profanity detection systems have helped, but have failed to address the problem of why this content is contributed in the first place.
sentences.A2: That is, what implications do interface design choices have on the content being generated?
sentences.A3: One such design choice is whether or not a site allows anonymous comments.
sentences.A4: What impact does allowing anonymity have on the quality or quantity of participation on a site?
sentences.A5: This case study analyses the impact of anonymity on a technology social news site, TechCrunch.com.
sentences.A6: TechCrunch is ideal for this study in that it underwent a shift from allowing anonymous comments (using the Disqus commenting platform) to disallowing them (using the Facebook commenting platform) in March of 2011.
sentences.A7: We compare the quality of anonymous and real identity comments through measures of reading level, relevance to the target article, negativity and presence of swear words and anger words.
sentences.A8: We couple this qualitative analysis with a quantitative analysis of the change in participation to give a complete picture of the impact of anonymity in this online community, with the end goal of informing design on similar social news sites.
sentences.T0: The Impact of Anonymity in Online Communities

title: The Impact of Anonymity in Online Communities

sentences.A0: Measures of semantic similarity between concepts are widely used in Natural Language Processing.
sentences.A1: In this article, we show how six existing domain-independent measures can be adapted to the biomedical domain.
sentences.A2: These measures were originally based on WordNet, an English lexical database of concepts and relations.
sentences.A3: In this research, we adapt these measures to the SNOMED-CT ontology of medical concepts.
sentences.A4: The measures include two path-based measures, and three measures that augment path-based measures with information content statistics from corpora.
sentences.A5: We also derive a context vector measure based on medical corpora that can be used as a measure of semantic relatedness.
sentences.A6: These six measures are evaluated against a newly created test bed of 30 medical concept pairs scored by three physicians and nine medical coders.
sentences.A7: We find that the medical coders and physicians differ in their ratings, and that the context vector measure correlates most closely with the physicians, while the path-based measures and one of the information content measures correlates most closely with the medical coders.
sentences.A8: We conclude that there is a role both for more flexible measures of relatedness based on information derived from corpora, as well as for measures that rely on existing ontological structures.
sentences.T0: Measures of semantic similarity and relatedness in the biomedical domain

title: Measures of semantic similarity and relatedness in the biomedical domain

sentences.A0: Interacting with computers is a ubiquitous activity for millions of people.
sentences.A1: Repetitive or specialized tasks often require creation of small, often one-off, programs.
sentences.A2: End-users struggle with learning and using the myriad of domain-specific languages (DSLs) to effectively accomplish these tasks.
sentences.A3: We present a general framework for constructing program synthesizers that take natural language (NL) inputs and produce expressions in a target DSL.
sentences.A4: The framework takes as input a DSL definition and training data consisting of NL/DSL pairs.
sentences.A5: From these it constructs a synthesizer by learning optimal weights and classifiers (using NLP features) that rank the outputs of a keyword-programming based translation.
sentences.A6: We applied our framework to three domains: repetitive text editing, an intelligent tutoring system, and flight information queries.
sentences.A7: On 1200+ English descriptions, the respective synthesizers rank the desired program as the top-1 and top-3 for 80% and 90% descriptions respectively.
sentences.T0: Program Synthesis using Natural Language

title: Program Synthesis using Natural Language

sentences.A0: The utilization of social media material in journalistic workflows is increasing, demanding automated methods for the identification of mis- and disinformation.
sentences.A1: Since textual contradiction across social media posts can be a signal of rumorousness, we seek to model how claims in Twitter posts are being textually contradicted.
sentences.A2: We identify two different contexts in which contradiction emerges: its broader form can be observed across independently posted tweets and its more specific form in threaded conversations.
sentences.A3: We define how the two scenarios differ in terms of central elements of argumentation: claims and conversation structure.
sentences.A4: We design and evaluate models for the two scenarios uniformly as 3-way Recognizing Textual Entailment tasks in order to represent claims and conversation structure implicitly in a generic inference model, while previous studies used explicit or no representation of these properties.
sentences.A5: To address noisy text, our classifiers use simple similarity features derived from the string and part-of-speech level.
sentences.A6: Corpus statistics reveal distribution differences for these features in contradictory as opposed to non-contradictory tweet relations, and the classifiers yield state of the art performance.
sentences.T0: Contradiction Detection for Rumorous Claims

title: Contradiction Detection for Rumorous Claims

sentences.A0: OBJECTIVE Literature-based discovery (LBD) aims to identify "hidden knowledge" in the medical literature by: (1) analyzing documents to identify pairs of explicitly related concepts (terms), then (2) hypothesizing novel relations between pairs of unrelated concepts that are implicitly related via a shared concept to which both are explicitly related.
sentences.A1: Many LBD approaches use simple techniques to identify semantically weak relations between concepts, for example, document co-occurrence.
sentences.A10: Using relations based on linguistic analysis generated many fewer hypotheses, but a significantly greater proportion of them were candidates for hidden knowledge.
sentences.A11: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION The use of linguistic analysis-based relations improves accuracy of LBD without overly damaging coverage.
sentences.A12: LBD systems often generate huge numbers of hypotheses, which are infeasible to manually review.
sentences.A13: Improving their accuracy has the potential to make these systems significantly more usable.
sentences.A2: These generate huge numbers of hypotheses, difficult for humans to assess.
sentences.A3: More complex techniques rely on linguistic analysis, for example, shallow parsing, to identify semantically stronger relations.
sentences.A4: Such approaches generate fewer hypotheses, but may miss hidden knowledge.
sentences.A5: The authors investigate this trade-off in detail, comparing techniques for identifying related concepts to discover which are most suitable for LBD.
sentences.A6: MATERIALS AND METHODS A generic LBD system that can utilize a range of relation types was developed.
sentences.A7: Experiments were carried out comparing a number of techniques for identifying relations.
sentences.A8: Two approaches were used for evaluation: replication of existing discoveries and the "time slicing" approach.
sentences.A9: (1) RESULTS: Previous LBD discoveries could be replicated using relations based either on document co-occurrence or linguistic analysis.
sentences.T0: Exploring relation types for literature-based discovery

title: Exploring relation types for literature-based discovery

sentences.A0: This paper describes an algorithm for automatically interpreting noun sequences in unrestricted text.
sentences.A1: This system uses broadcoverage semantic information which has been acquired automatically by analyzing the definitions in an on-line dictionary.
sentences.A2: Previously, computational studies of noun sequences made use of hand-coded semantic information, and they applied the analysis rules sequentially.
sentences.A3: In contrast, the task of analyzing noun sequences in unrestricted text strongly favors an algorithm according to which the rules are applied in parallel and the best interpretation is determined by weights associated with rule applications.
sentences.T0: Algorithm For Automatic Interpretation Of Noun Sequences

title: Algorithm For Automatic Interpretation Of Noun Sequences

sentences.A0: This research compares several of the thematic roles of Verb Net (VN) to those of the Linguistic Infrastructure for Interoperable Resources and Systems (LIRICS).
sentences.A1: The purpose of this comparison is to develop a standard set of thematic roles that would be suited to a variety of natural language processing (NLP) applications.
sentences.A2: We draw from both resources to construct a unified set of semantic roles that will replace existing VN semantic roles.
sentences.A3: Through the process of comparison, we find that a hierarchical organization of coarse-grained, intermediate and fine-grained roles facilitates mapping between semantic resources of differing granularity and allows for flexibility in how VN can be used for diverse NLP applications, thus, we propose a hierarchical taxonomy of the unified role set.
sentences.A4: The comparison and subsequent development of the hierarchy reveals a level of granularity shared by both resources, which could be further developed into a standard set of thematic roles for the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).
sentences.T0: A Hierarchical Unification of LIRICS and VerbNet Semantic Roles

title: A Hierarchical Unification of LIRICS and VerbNet Semantic Roles

sentences.A0: We propose a generic, memory-based approach for the detection of implicit semantic roles.
sentences.A1: While state-of-the-art methods for this task combine hand-crafted rules with specialized and costly lexical resources, our models use large corpora with automated annotations for explicit semantic roles only to capture the distribution of predicates and their associated roles.
sentences.A2: We show that memory-based learning can increase the recognition rate of implicit roles beyond the state-of-the-art.
sentences.T0: Memory-Based Acquisition of Argument Structures and its Application to Implicit Role Detection

title: Memory-Based Acquisition of Argument Structures and its Application to Implicit Role Detection

sentences.A0: Grammatical agreement flags the parts of sentences that belong together regardless of whether the parts appear together.
sentences.A1: In English, the major agreement controller is the sentence subject, the major agreement targets are verbs and pronouns, and the major agreement category is number.
sentences.A2: The authors expand an account of number agreement whose tenets are that pronouns acquire number lexically, whereas verbs acquire it syntactically but with similar contributions from number meaning and from the number morphology of agreement controllers.
sentences.A3: These tenets were instantiated in a model using existing verb agreement data.
sentences.A4: The model was then fit to a new, more extensive set of verb data and tested with a parallel set of pronoun data.
sentences.A5: The theory was supported by the model's outcomes.
sentences.A6: The results have implications for the integration of words and structures, for the workings of agreement categories, and for the nature of the transition from thought to language.
sentences.T0: Making syntax of sense: number agreement in sentence production.

title: Making syntax of sense: number agreement in sentence production.

sentences.A0: Unsolicited commercial email (UCE), also known as spam, has been a major problem on the Internet.
sentences.A1: In the past, researchers have addressed this problem as a text classification or categorization problem.
sentences.A2: However, as spammers' techniques continue to evolve and the genre of email content becomes more and more diverse, text-based anti-spam approaches alone are no longer sufficient.
sentences.A3: In this paper, we propose a novel anti-spam system which utilizes visual clues, in addition to text information in the email body, to determine whether a message is spam.
sentences.A4: We analyze a large collection of spam emails containing images and identify a number of useful visual features for this application.
sentences.A5: We then propose using one-class support vector machines (SVM) as the underlying base classifier for anti-spam filtering.
sentences.A6: The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system can add significant filtering power to the existing text-based anti-spam filters.
sentences.T0: Using visual features for anti-spam filtering

title: Using visual features for anti-spam filtering

sentences.A0: We present BEAMER: a new spatially exploitative approach to learning object detectors which shows excellent results when applied to the task of detecting objects in greyscale aerial imagery in the presence of ambiguous and noisy data.
sentences.A1: There are four main contributions used to produce these results.
sentences.A2: First, we introduce a grammar-guided feature extraction system, enabling the exploration of a richer feature space while constraining the features to a useful subset.
sentences.A3: This is specified with a rule-based generative grammar crafted by a human expert.
sentences.A4: Second, we learn a classifier on this data using a newly proposed variant of AdaBoost which takes into account the spatially correlated nature of the data.
sentences.A5: Third, we perform another round of training to optimize the method of converting the pixel classifications generated by boosting into a high quality set of (x, y) locations.
sentences.A6: Lastly, we carefully define three common problems in object detection and define two evaluation criteria that are tightly matched to these problems.
sentences.A7: Major strengths of this approach are: (1) a way of randomly searching a broad feature space, (2) its performance when evaluated on well-matched evaluation criteria, and (3) its use of the location prediction domain to learn object detectors as well as to generate detections that perform well on several tasks: object counting, tracking, and target detection.
sentences.A8: We demonstrate the efficacy of BEAMER with a comprehensive experimental evaluation on a challenging data set.
sentences.T0: Learning Object Location Predictors with Boosting and Grammar-Guided Feature Extraction

title: Learning Object Location Predictors with Boosting and Grammar-Guided Feature Extraction

sentences.A0: As the world becomes more reliant on Web applications for commercial, financial, and medical transactions, cyber attacks on the World Wide Web are increasing in frequency and severity.
sentences.A1: Web applications provide an attractive alternative to traditional desktop applications due to their accessibility and ease of deployment.
sentences.A10: In addition, our approach has a number of desirable characteristics, including robustness to missing contextual information, interpretability of models, and scalability.
sentences.A2: However, the accessibility of Web applications also makes them extremely vulnerable to attack.
sentences.A3: This inherent vulnerability is intensified by the distributed nature of Web applications and the complexity of configuring application servers.
sentences.A4: These factors have led to a proliferation of Web-based attacks, in which attackers surreptitiously inject code into HTTP requests, allowing them to execute arbitrary commands on remote systems and perform malicious activities such as reading, altering, or destroying sensitive data.
sentences.A5: One approach for dealing with HTTP-based attacks is to identify malicious code in incoming HTTP requests and eliminate bad requests before they are processed.
sentences.A6: Using machine learning techniques, we can build a classifier to automatically label requests as “Valid” or “Attack.” For this study, we develop a simple, but effective HTTP attack classifier, based on the vector space model used commonly for Information Retrieval.
sentences.A7: Our classifier not only separates attacks from valid requests, but can also identify specific attack types (e.g., “SQL Injection” or “Path Traversal”).
sentences.A8: We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on the ECML/PKDD 2007 Discovery Challenge data set.
sentences.A9: Specifically, we show that our approach achieves higher precision and recall than previous methods.
sentences.T0: Classification of HTTP Attacks: A Study on the ECML/PKDD 2007 Discovery Challenge

title: Classification of HTTP Attacks: A Study on the ECML/PKDD 2007 Discovery Challenge

sentences.A0: Subjectivity in natural language refers to aspects of language used to express opinions and evaluations (Banfield, 1982; Wiebe, 1994).
sentences.A1: There are numerous applications for which knowledge of subjectivity is relevant, including genre detection, information extraction, and information retrieval.
sentences.A2: This paper shows promising results for a straightforward method of identifying collocational clues of subjectivity, as well as evidence of the usefulness of these clues for recognizing opinionated documents.
sentences.T0: Identifying Collocations for Recognizing Opinions

title: Identifying Collocations for Recognizing Opinions

sentences.A0: Markov decision processes (MDPs) are a well studied framework for solving sequential decision making problems under uncertainty.
sentences.A1: Exact methods for solving MDPs based on dynamic programming such as policy iteration and value iteration are effective on small problems.
sentences.A2: In problems with a large discrete state space or with continuous state spaces, a compact representation is essential for providing an efficient approximation solutions to MDPs.
sentences.A3: Commonly used approximation algorithms involving constructing basis functions for projecting the value function onto a low dimensional subspace, and building a factored or hierarchical graphical model to decompose the transition and reward functions.
sentences.A4: However, hand-coding a good compact representation for a given reinforcement learning (RL) task can be quite difficult and time consuming.
sentences.A5: Recent approaches have attempted to automatically discover efficient representations for RL.
sentences.A6: In this thesis proposal, we discuss the problems of automatically constructing structured kernel for kernel based RL, a popular approach to learning non-parametric approximations for value function.
sentences.A7: We explore a space of kernel structures which are built compositionally from base kernels using a context-free grammar.
sentences.A8: We examine a greedy algorithm for searching over the structure space.
sentences.A9: To demonstrate how the learned structure can represent and approximate the original RL problem in terms of compactness and efficiency, we plan to evaluate our method on a synthetic problem and compare it to other RL baselines.
sentences.T0: Learning Efficient Representations for Reinforcement Learning

title: Learning Efficient Representations for Reinforcement Learning

sentences.A0: We report grammar inference experiments on partially parsed sentences taken from the Wall Street Journal corpus using the inside-outside algorithm for stochastic context-free grammars.
sentences.A1: The initial grammar for the inference process makes no assumption of the kinds of structures and their distributions.
sentences.A2: The inferred grammar is evaluated by its predicting power and by comparing the bracketing of held out sentences imposed by the inferred grammar with the partial bracketings of these sentences given in the corpus.
sentences.A3: Using part-of-speech tags as the only source of lexical information, high bracketing accuracy is achieved even with a small subset of the available training material (1045 sentences): 94.4% for test sentences shorter than 10 words and 90.2% for sentences shorter than 15 words.
sentences.T0: Parsing the Wall Street Journal with the Inside-Outside Algorithm

title: Parsing the Wall Street Journal with the Inside-Outside Algorithm

sentences.A0: In language-oriented programming and modeling, software developers are largely concerned with the definition of domain-specific languages (DSLs) and their composition.
sentences.A1: While various implementation techniques and frameworks exist for defining DSLs, language composition has not obtained enough attention and is not well-enough understood.
sentences.A2: In particular, there is a lack of precise terminology for describing observations about language composition in theory and in existing language-development systems.
sentences.A3: To clarify the issue, we specify five forms of language composition: language extension, language restriction, language unification, self-extension, and extension composition.
sentences.A4: We illustrate this classification by various examples and apply it to discuss the performance of different language-development systems with respect to language composition.
sentences.A5: We hope that the terminology provided by our classification will enable more precise communication on language composition.
sentences.T0: Language composition untangled

title: Language composition untangled

sentences.A0: Document images often suffer from different types of degradation that renders the document image binarization a challenging task.
sentences.A1: This paper presents a document image binarization technique that segments the text from badly degraded document images accurately.
sentences.A2: The proposed technique is based on the observations that the text documents usually have a document background of the uniform color and texture and the document text within it has a different intensity level compared with the surrounding document background.
sentences.A3: Given a document image, the proposed technique first estimates a document background surface through an iterative polynomial smoothing procedure.
sentences.A4: Different types of document degradation are then compensated by using the estimated document background surface.
sentences.A5: The text stroke edge is further detected from the compensated document image by using L1-norm image gradient.
sentences.A6: Finally, the document text is segmented by a local threshold that is estimated based on the detected text stroke edges.
sentences.A7: The proposed technique was submitted to the recent document image binarization contest (DIBCO) held under the framework of ICDAR 2009 and has achieved the top performance among 43 algorithms that are submitted from 35 international research groups.
sentences.T0: Document image binarization using background estimation and stroke edges

title: Document image binarization using background estimation and stroke edges

sentences.A0: General treebank analyses are graph structured, but parsers are typically restricted to tree structures for efficiency and modeling reasons.
sentences.A1: We propose a new representation and algorithm for a class of graph structures that is flexible enough to cover almost all treebank structures, while still admitting efficient learning and inference.
sentences.A2: In particular, we consider directed, acyclic, one-endpoint-crossing graph structures, which cover most long-distance dislocation, shared argumentation, and similar tree-violating linguistic phenomena.
sentences.A3: We describe how to convert phrase structure parses, including traces, to our new representation in a reversible manner.
sentences.A4: Our dynamic program uniquely decomposes structures, is sound and complete, and covers 97.3% of the Penn English Treebank.
sentences.A5: We also implement a proof-of-concept parser that recovers a range of null elements and trace types.
sentences.T0: Parsing with Traces: An $O(n^4)$ Algorithm and a Structural Representation

title: Parsing with Traces: An $O(n^4)$ Algorithm and a Structural Representation

sentences.A0: The string-to-string correction problem is to determine the distance between two strings as measured by the minimum cost sequence of “edit operations” needed to change the one string into the other.
sentences.A1: The edit operations investigated allow changing one symbol of a string into another single symbol, deleting one symbol from a string, or inserting a single symbol into a string.
sentences.A2: An algorithm is presented which solves this problem in time proportional to the product of the lengths of the two strings.
sentences.A3: Possible applications are to the problems of automatic spelling correction and determining the longest subsequence of characters common to two strings.
sentences.T0: The String-to-String Correction Problem

title: The String-to-String Correction Problem

sentences.A0: This paper describes a methodology for semi-supervised learning of dialogue acts using the similarity between sentences.
sentences.A1: We suppose that the dialogue sentences with the same dialogue act are more similar in terms of semantic and syntactic information.
sentences.A2: However, previous work on sentence similarity mainly modeled a sentence as bag-of-words and then compared different groups of words using corpus-based or knowledge-based measurements of word semantic similarity.
sentences.A3: Novelly, we present a vector-space sentence representation, composed of word embeddings, that is, the related word distributed representations, and these word embeddings are organised in a sentence syntactic structure.
sentences.A4: Given the vectors of the dialogue sentences, a distance measurement can be well-defined to compute the similarity between them.
sentences.A5: Finally, a seeded k-means clustering algorithm is implemented to classify the dialogue sentences into several categories corresponding to particular dialogue acts.
sentences.A6: This constitutes the semi-supervised nature of the approach, which aims to ameliorate the reliance of the availability of annotated corpora.
sentences.A7: Experiments with Switchboard Dialog Act corpus show that classification accuracy is improved by 14%, compared to the state-of-art methods based on Support Vector Machine.
sentences.T0: Semi-supervised learning of dialogue acts using sentence similarity based on word embeddings

title: Semi-supervised learning of dialogue acts using sentence similarity based on word embeddings

sentences.A0: AbstractWe present a new hierarchical Bayesian model for unsupervised topic segmentation.
sentences.A1: This new model integrates a point-wise boundary sampling algorithm used in Bayesian segmentation into a structured topic model that can capture a simple hierarchical topic structure latent in documents.
sentences.A2: We develop an MCMC inference algorithm to split/merge segment(s).
sentences.A3: Experimental results show that our model outperforms previous unsupervised segmentation methods using only lexical information on Choi's datasets and two meeting transcripts and has performance comparable to those previous methods on two written datasets.
sentences.T0: Topic Segmentation with a Structured Topic Model

title: Topic Segmentation with a Structured Topic Model

sentences.A0: Hateful and offensive language (also known as hate speech or cyber hate) posted and widely circulated via the World Wide Web can be considered as a key risk factor for individual and societal tension linked to regional instability.
sentences.A1: Automated Web-based hate speech detection is important for the observation and understanding trends of societal tension.
sentences.A2: In this research, we improve on existing research by proposing different data mining feature extraction methods.
sentences.A3: While previous work has involved using lexicons, bags-of-words or probabilistic parsing approach (e.g. using Typed Dependencies), they all suffer from a similar issue which is that hate speech can often be subtle and indirect, and depending on individual words or phrases can lead to a significant number of false negatives.
sentences.A4: This problem motivated us to conduct new experiments to identify subtle language use, such as references to immigration or job prosperity in a hateful context.
sentences.A5: We propose a novel 'Othering Lexicon' to identify these subtleties and we incorporate our lexicon with embedding learning for feature extraction and subsequent classification using a neural network approach.
sentences.A6: Our method first explores the context around othering terms in a corpus, and identifies context patterns that are relevant to the othering context.
sentences.A7: These patterns are used along with the othering pronoun and hate speech terms to build our 'Othering Lexicon'.
sentences.A8: Embedding algorithm has the superior characteristic that the similar words have a closer distance, which is helpful to train our classifier on the negative and positive classes.
sentences.A9: For validation, several experiments were conducted on different types of hate speech, namely religion, disability, race and sexual orientation, with F-measure scores for classifying hateful instances obtained through applying our model of 0.93, 0.95, 0.97 and 0.92 respective.
sentences.T0: ’ The Enemy Among Us ’ : Detecting Hate Speech with Threats Based Othering Language Embeddings

title: ’ The Enemy Among Us ’ : Detecting Hate Speech with Threats Based Othering Language Embeddings

sentences.A0: Image annotation is a process of finding appropriate semantic labels for images in order to obtain a more convenient way for indexing and searching images on the Web.
sentences.A1: This article proposes a novel method for image annotation based on combining feature-word distributions, which map from visual space to word space, and word-topic distributions, which form a structure to capture label relationships for annotation.
sentences.A2: We refer to this type of model as Feature-Word-Topic models.
sentences.A3: The introduction of topics allows us to efficiently take word associations, such as {ocean, fish, coral} or {desert, sand, cactus}, into account for image annotation.
sentences.A4: Unlike previous topic-based methods, we do not consider topics as joint distributions of words and visual features, but as distributions of words only.
sentences.A5: Feature-word distributions are utilized to define weights in computation of topic distributions for annotation.
sentences.A6: By doing so, topic models in text mining can be applied directly in our method.
sentences.A7: Our Feature-word-topic model, which exploits Gaussian Mixtures for feature-word distributions, and probabilistic Latent Semantic Analysis (pLSA) for word-topic distributions, shows that our method is able to obtain promising results in image annotation and retrieval.
sentences.T0: A feature-word-topic model for image annotation and retrieval

title: A feature-word-topic model for image annotation and retrieval

sentences.A0: Information mining from networks by identifying communities is an important problem across a number of research fields including social science, biology, physics, and medicine.
sentences.A1: Most existing community detection algorithms are graph theoretic and lack the ability to detect accurate community boundaries if the ratio of intra-community to inter-community links is low.
sentences.A2: Also, algorithms based on modularity maximization may fail to resolve communities smaller than a specific size if the community size varies significantly.
sentences.A3: In this paper, we present a fundamentally different community detection algorithm based on the fact that each network community spans a different subspace in the geodesic space.
sentences.A4: Therefore, each node can only be efficiently represented as a linear combination of nodes spanning the same subspace.
sentences.A5: To make the process of community detection more robust, we use sparse linear coding with l1 norm constraint.
sentences.A6: In order to find a community label for each node, sparse spectral clustering algorithm is used.
sentences.A7: The proposed community detection technique is compared with more than 10 state of the art methods on two benchmark networks (with known clusters) using normalized mutual information criterion.
sentences.A8: Our proposed algorithm outperformed existing algorithms with a significant margin on both benchmark networks.
sentences.A9: The proposed algorithm has also shown excellent performance on three real-world networks.
sentences.T0: Subspace Based Network Community Detection Using Sparse Linear Coding

title: Subspace Based Network Community Detection Using Sparse Linear Coding

sentences.A0: Learning languages in addition to the native language is very important for all people in the globalized world today, and computer-aided pronunciation training (CAPT) is attractive since the software can be used anywhere at any time, and repeated as many times as desired.
sentences.A1: In this paper, we introduce the immersive interaction scenario offered by spoken dialogues to CAPT by proposing a recursive dialogue game to make CAPT personalized.
sentences.A2: A number of tree-structured sub-dialogues are linked sequentially and recursively as the script for the game.
sentences.A3: The system policy at each dialogue turn is to select in real-time along the dialogue the best training sentence for each specific individual learner within the dialogue script, considering the learner's learning status and the future possible dialogue paths in the script, such that the learner can have the scores for all pronunciation units considered reaching a predefined standard in a minimum number of turns.
sentences.A4: The purpose here is that those pronunciation units poorly produced by the specific learner can be offered with more practice opportunities in the future sentences along the dialogue, which enables the learner to improve the pronunciation without having to repeat the same training sentences many times.
sentences.A5: This makes the learning process for each learner completely personalized.
sentences.A6: The dialogue policy is modeled by Markov decision process (MDP) with high-dimensional continuous state space, and trained with fitted value iteration using a huge number of simulated learners.
sentences.A7: These simulated leaners have the behavior similar to real learners, and were generated from a corpus of real learner data.
sentences.A8: The experiments demonstrated very promising results and a real cloud-based system is also successfully implemented.
sentences.T0: A Recursive Dialogue Game for Personalized Computer-Aided Pronunciation Training

title: A Recursive Dialogue Game for Personalized Computer-Aided Pronunciation Training

sentences.A0: Developing systems that motivate people to change their behaviors, such as an exercise application for the smartphone, is challenging.
sentences.A1: One solution is to implement motivational strategies from existing behavior change theory and tailor these strategies to preferences based on personal characteristics, like personality and gender.
sentences.A2: We operationalized strategies by collecting representative motivational text messages and aligning the messages to ten theory-based behavior change strategies.
sentences.A3: We conducted an online survey with 350 participants, where the participants rated 50 of our text messages (each aligned to one of the ten strategies) on how motivating they found them.
sentences.A4: Results show that differences in personality and gender relate to significant differences in the evaluations of nine out of ten strategies.
sentences.A5: Eight out of ten strategies were perceived as either more or less motivating in relation to scores on the personality traits Openness, Extraversion, and Agreeableness.
sentences.A6: Four strategies were perceived as more motivating by men than by women.
sentences.A7: These findings show that personality and gender influence how motivational strategies are perceived.
sentences.A8: We conclude that our theory-based behavior change strategies can be more motivating by tailoring them to personality and gender of users of behavior change systems.
sentences.T0: A word of advice: how to tailor motivational text messages based on behavior change theory to personality and gender

title: A word of advice: how to tailor motivational text messages based on behavior change theory to personality and gender

sentences.A0: We present a supervised hyperspectral image segmentation algorithm based on a convex formulation of a marginal maximum a posteriori segmentation with hidden fields and structure tensor regularization: Segmentation via the Constraint Split Augmented Lagrangian Shrinkage by Structure Tensor Regularization (SegSALSA-STR).

sentences.A0: We present Emergent, a novel data-set derived from a digital journalism project for rumour debunking.

sentences.A0: This article presents work in progress towards a better understanding of the origins of narrative.

sentences.A0: This article compares the predictions of two models of grammatical encoding in language production.

sentences.A0: We present and evaluate a novel approach to natural language generation (NLG) in statistical spoken dialogue systems (SDS) using a data-driven statistical optimization framework for incremental information presentation (IP), where there is a trade-off to be solved between presenting “enough" information to the user while keeping the utterances short and understandable.

sentences.A0: This work explores how internal representations of modern statistical machine translation systems can be exploited for cross-language information retrieval.

sentences.A4: Both are context-sensitive, in contrast to a baseline context-insensitive approach that uses bilingual dictionaries for word-by-word translation.
sentences.A5: Experimental results show that by “opening up” modern statistical machine translation systems, we can access intermediate representations that yield high retrieval effectiveness.
